head: d3dc4c2c6
summary: Walk-in resolver is a clean, idempotent SSOT (firstOrCreate by stable email sentinel walkingcustomer@example.com). Receipt path was just successfully refactored to flow through ReceiptDataService (delegated by OrderDetailsResource) so the six NF525 header fields converge on a single producer. The recent typehint widening from `Order` to `BroadcastableOrder` (commit d3dc4c2c6) restores kiosk checkout (FrontendOrder accepted) without breaking POS. Architecture is sound; observations are mainly about scattered duplication of payment-line/PII concerns and one legacy receipt component that does NOT share the NF525 footer/duplicata-marker contract.

findings.title: ReceiptDataService SSOT contract is now enforced by sentinel tests
findings.evidence: OrderDetailsResource L24 calls `app(ReceiptDataService::class)->buildForOrderModel($this->resource)` and uses the returned array for fiscal_sequence_no, pos_register_id, pos_siret, pos_vat_intra, pos_legal_footer, operator_name (L80-86). The new test `test_order_details_resource_delegates_nf525_fields_to_receipt_data_service` locks this delegation by asserting field-by-field equality with the service output. `test_legacy_buildForOrder_and_new_buildForOrderModel_are_equivalent` keeps the two service signatures aligned. `test_build_for_order_model_accepts_frontend_order_sibling` locks the BroadcastableOrder typehint widening.
findings.recommendation: Keep these tests in CI smoke pipeline — they are the only thing preventing a regression where a future patch reads `$this->branch->siret` directly from the resource.

findings.title: PosOrderReceiptComponent (re-print history modal) does NOT use ReceiptDuplicataMarker or NF525 footer
findings.evidence: This component (admin/posOrders surface — re-print from order history) renders a paper-receipt block but neither imports nor mounts <receipt-duplicata-marker>, and never reads order.fiscal_sequence_no, order.pos_siret, order.pos_vat_intra, order.pos_register_id, order.operator_name, order.pos_legal_footer, order.tax_lines, or buildNf525Footer(). Compare with ReceiptComponent.vue L67-73 (header siret/vat/register/operator) + L74 (duplicata marker) + L241-247 (NF525 footer loop). Result: a manager re-printing a ticket from the orders history will produce a receipt missing fiscal_sequence_no + duplicata mark — a NF525 hole on the legally-most-sensitive print path (re-impression). The fiscal increment endpoint is also not invoked from this component, so receipt_print_count never advances from this surface.
findings.recommendation: P2 because the day-to-day re-print path (from PosOrdersTrackerComponent → ReceiptComponent) IS correct. But manager-side re-print from /admin/posOrders should either (a) redirect to the ReceiptComponent path or (b) be brought to feature-parity with NF525 header + duplicata + POST print-receipt. Track for V1.0.2 — owner Aurore needs to confirm which path managers actually use.

findings.title: Payment-lines normalisation lives in TWO places
findings.evidence: Both `formatPaymentsBreakdown` (JS, posReceiptBuilder L34-57) and `buildPaymentsBreakdown` (PHP, OrderDetailsResource L114-158) implement the same fallback ladder: (1) array of payments → enriched lines, (2) single tender from pos_payment_method/pos_received_amount → synthetic 1-line array, (3) empty. They are factual duplicates serving the same UX (the PHP one feeds payments_breakdown into the API response, the JS one normalises that same array for rendering + handles the pre-payment LIVE tranche case). Risk: future change to single-tender semantics has to be made in both layers.
findings.recommendation: Not a defect today (PHP is for persisted orders, JS adds the LIVE-tranche helper). Document the contract in a header comment so the next maintainer doesn't drop one of the two layers.

findings.title: WalkInCustomerResolver is firstOrCreate-only — DB-first idempotent
findings.evidence: L16-37 use a single firstOrCreate keyed by email=walkingcustomer@example.com. branch_id=0 makes the walk-in user globally visible across BranchScope (admin tenant). The PENDING_WALKIN phone sentinel is documented (L23-31) as both NOT-NULL-satisfier and ValidPhone-failer — meaning any accidental DELIVERY flow that reuses this user would be rejected by the phone validator. ensureCustomerRole (L44-57) lazily assigns the `Customer` role with a Throwable guard so role-seed-absent test contexts don't blow up. Two callers: `walkInCustomer()` HTTP action (PosController L149-162, throttled 120/min on pos-quote limiter) and the implicit normalize in `normalizePosRuntimePayload` (PosController L224-228).
findings.recommendation: Clean. Consider documenting the contract that any code creating a User via this email is a bug (only this service may), and add a DB-level UNIQUE assertion to the integration test.

findings.title: Increment endpoint atomic — no race window in concurrent multi-station reprint
findings.evidence: L43-48 use `Order::query()->whereKey($order)->where('branch_id', $branchId)->update(['receipt_print_count' => DB::raw('COALESCE(receipt_print_count, 0) + 1')])` — a single SQL UPDATE statement makes concurrent prints from two stations safe (each statement is atomic in MySQL row-locking). The subsequent SELECT (L54-58) re-reads with the same tenant filter (defense in depth on top of BranchScope). The audit emission is wrapped in try/catch (L77-104) so a chain failure does NOT block the cashier from delivering the paper ticket — operational continuity is documented (L26-28).
findings.recommendation: Strong design. The `audit_emitted=false` signal in the response (L73) is the right escape hatch — SIEM can subscribe. Verify that the frontend surfaces this to the operator (today ReceiptComponent.vue's handlePrintClientClick ignores it — see UX/A11y report).

findings.title: Receipt rate limit asymmetry — 120/min on the GET walk-in lookup, NO throttle on the POST print-receipt fiscal increment
findings.evidence: Line 752-758 of routes/api.php: walk-in-customer GET + quote POST both wear `throttle:pos-quote` (120/min). Line 831: `Route::post('/orders/{order}/print-receipt', [PosReceiptPrintController::class, 'increment'])->middleware('idempotency')->name('orders.print-receipt')` — only the idempotency middleware, NO rate-limit. With per-user throttling at 120/min on the broader bucket `api/admin/pos/*` (RouteServiceProvider.php L86-88), the global `api` group bucket would still cap an abusive operator at ~120 RPM, but a misbehaving frontend (re-entrant click loop) could write 120 audit_log rows per minute per operator. Not a security DoS, but a fiscal chain noise risk.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2: add `throttle:pos-quote` to print-receipt route (or a tighter dedicated limiter like 30/min, since human-paced reprint is rare). The Vue component does have a re-entrant guard (isPrinting + 3 rapid-clicks → 1 call in the spec), so the risk is bounded today.

findings.title: effectiveOrder computed prefers max(local, prop) — anti-flicker correct
findings.evidence: ReceiptComponent.vue L421-431 computes `effectiveCount = Math.max(baseCount, localCount)` so a parent prop refetch returning the older count cannot make the DUPLICATA badge disappear after a successful print bump. Tested by spec L129-141 (`effectiveOrder follows parent prop changes after the local bump`).
